findings.passage: People should be able to vote without photo identification. Strongly Disagree
findings.note: iVoterGuide candidate questionnaire page for the 2022 Kentucky primary (May 17, 2022); the date the answer was given is not printed. Ticked answer to the statement 'People should be able to vote without photo identification.' is 'Strongly Disagree'.

findings.passage: I would remove the use of non-photo ids to vote.  I would support exploring the use of block-chain technology to create fraud proof elections that still allow for anonymous voting in our elections.
findings.note: Written answer on the same iVoterGuide 2022 primary page, to the question 'What laws would you propose to change present voting practices?'. Date of answer not printed.

findings.note: iVoterGuide page for the 2022 Kentucky general election (Nov 8, 2022); ticked answer 'Strongly Disagree'. The same page shows 'Did not answer' for the free-text question on changes to voting practices. Date of answer not printed.

findings.passage: People should be able to vote without photo identification. Strongly Agree
findings.note: iVoterGuide page for the 2024 Kentucky primary (May 21, 2024); ticked answer 'Strongly Agree'. The page is marked as 'Public data' and shows '(Candidate did not provide)' in its biography section, and it conflicts with the 2022 and 2026 pages. The staff note on the 2024 general-election page for this person says the intended answer was the opposite (see that finding). Date of answer not printed.

findings.passage: Staff note: After evaluations occurred, candidate notified iVoterGuide that the intended answer to this question should have been: STRONGLY DISAGREE.
findings.note: iVoterGuide page for the 2024 Kentucky general election (Nov 5, 2024). The ticked answer printed to 'People should be able to vote without photo identification.' is 'Strongly Agree', and the page's staff note says the candidate told iVoterGuide after evaluation that the intended answer was Strongly Disagree. The note is iVoterGuide's report of what the candidate told them, not a direct candidate quote.
